sophia_prod: FYI customer AcmePay reporting high 504 rates and big tail latency spikes on hosted API since ~21:37 UTC. They say many requests show '504 Gateway Timeout' and some 502s. Customer seeing failure rate ~8%.

sophia_prod: Quick snapshot from their request logs they pasted: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"long doc","max_tokens":1024}'` returns 504 reproducible in ~30s.

jordan_oncall: Oncall here. Observing matching internal alerts: request-queue-depth for gw-az1 jumped to 95% of limit at 21:35, continuous-batcher backlog increased, dequeue latency p95 -> 5s then many 30s timeouts.

carla_sre: Logs show batcher queues piling for tenant acmepay-tenant-id. Relevant excerpts: 
```
[21:36:12] batcher: enqueue req tenant=acmepay len=1024 tokens seq=1
[21:36:12] batcher: batch_slice wait_count=48
[21:36:30] request-queue: depth=389/400 evict_policy=reject => 504
[21:37:05] kvcache: miss_rate=0.82 increasing kvcache-load
```

mike_infra: Looks like long-context generation (max_tokens 1024) + many concurrent requests triggered continuous batching backlog. Queue depth limit 400 hit; requests being early-rejected -> 504s.

elaine_support: Customer says this started after they released a background worker that fanouts many long-gen calls in parallel. They've paused that job for now.

jordan_oncall: Immediate mitigations we can do: 1) Temporarily increase gateway queue depth for the affected AZ (risk: memory), 2) Route acmepay tenant to dedicated fallback model with lower max_batch_size, 3) Apply tenant-level rate limit to reduce concurrency. Which option do we want now?

carla_sre: Recommend: apply rate limit + lower per-request max_tokens via routing (we can insert a policy to cap to 512 for this tenant) to reduce batch size. Also enable batching window reduction: set batch_max_wait_ms from 30 -> 10 in the batcher config for gw-az1 to avoid long tail waits.

mike_infra: I can bump queue depth from 400 -> 600 temporarily and spin up one extra batcher pod in gw-az1. Doing that now (ETA ~2m). Will monitor memory.

ops-bot: deploy request accepted by infra. Action: scale batcher gw-az1 +1 replica (triggered by mike_infra).

carla_sre: Added a conservative tenant policy to throttle acmepay to 6 concurrent requests and cap max_tokens=512. Also set batch_max_wait_ms=12 for that pool. Should reduce KV pressure.

elaine_support: Sent customer a temporary guidance note: "We've applied a rate limit and reduced per-request max_tokens to mitigate the timeouts. Please coordinate if you plan to ramp again." They confirmed reduced error rate to ~1.2% after the change.

jordan_oncall: Monitoring: queue depth dropped to 40% within 90s, dequeue p95 down to 1200ms, 504s decreasing. We'll keep the temporary changes for 2 hours and then assess.

carla_sre: Postmortem notes to capture: root cause = tenant-driven high concurrency of long-context requests causing continuous batching backlog + KV cache churn + queue-depth early rejects. Remediation = tenant rate limiting, cap max_tokens, reduce batch wait window, temporary queue depth bump, offer dedicated capacity if they need sustained throughput. Follow-up: add a targeted alert for kvcache miss_rate>0.6 + queue_depth>70% to catch earlier.

jordan_oncall: Assigning to sla-owners: @mike_infra for infra changes, @carla_sre for batcher config and runbook updates, @elaine_support for customer comms. Will update this thread after 2h observation.

deploy-bot: auto-note: infra scale completed at 5987654330. Batcher pod id: batcher-gw-az1-7f9cd added.

sophia_prod: Thanks all. Customer follow-up scheduled; will keep this thread open for the postmortem. :thumbsup:
